Subject: Exploring dedicated capacity + MAP for evaluation

Hi Hannah / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. CloudElevate is keen to evaluate Redwood Dedicated for a month-long PoC focused on low-latency search reranking and chat assistants (models: LlamaX-13B / Falcon-40B). We need a clear mutual action plan so procurement can approve the reserved capacity and get terms in place. High-level asks: 

- Target throughput: ~200 reqs/s aggregate, 128 token average per request
- Latency SLO: p95 < 120ms for simple completions
- Evaluation window: 4 weeks (PoC) + 4 weeks validation in staging
- Preferred region: us-west

Could you send a MAP with milestone dates, suggested GPU pool sizing, term/commit options, and burst behavior if we exceed baseline? Also include pricing tiers and what a 6 vs 12 vs 24 month reservation looks like.

Procurement contact will be Marcus Liu (cc'd) — they'll need a ballpark cost for budgeting. We're hoping to close the contract by mid-May if the PoC looks good.

Thanks,
Anya
CTO, CloudElevate
Mobile: +1 415-555-0198

Hi Anya — great to meet you and thanks for the clear asks. I've sketched a proposed MAP and attached a PDF (CloudElevate_MAP_v1.pdf). Key highlights below; full milestone table in the attachment.

Proposed MAP (summary):
- Week 0: Kickoff + access provisioning (VPC peering, IP allowlist, onboarding runbook)
- Weeks 1–4: PoC evaluation (dedicated 8-GPU pool, continuous prefix caching enabled)
  - Objective: reach 200 reqs/s with p95 latency target for the chosen models
- Weeks 5–8: Staging validation and metrics handoff (billing simulation + production smoke)
- Week 9: Decision & contract execution (if pass -> reserve capacity)

Sizing suggestion: 8 x A100 equivalent baseline for the PoC (estimated sustained throughput with batching). For production commits we recommend 16 GPUs baseline with staged ramp to 32 GPUs over 8 weeks.

Attach: CloudElevate_MAP_v1.pdf (MAP + milestone dates), Reservation_Pricing_Options.xlsx (baseline pricing scenarios).

Next steps: Ben will follow up on pricing and burst clauses; Karthik can outline the technical validation checklist and SOC2 evidence we’ll provide. Marcus — we’ll include a simple procurement timeline in the MAP.

Anya — following up with concrete pricing buckets and reservation terms (see attached spreadsheet). Short summary here so you can share with procurement: 

Reservation options (baseline pricing, USD/month):
- 8-GPU baseline (PoC): $58,000/mo (month-to-month evaluation pricing; billed pro-rata)
- 16-GPU reserved, 12-month term: $280,000/mo (15% discount vs month-to-month)
- 16-GPU reserved, 24-month term: $240,000/mo (25% discount, commit-based)
- 32-GPU reserved, 24-month term: $460,000/mo (volume discount applied)

Burst clauses (summary):
- Soft burst: +50% capacity available for short windows (max 2 hours/day) at 2x baseline unit rate
- Hard burst: additional capacity up to 100% with 24-hour notice at negotiated overage rate (1.5x baseline for committed customers)
- Auto-fallback: If reserved pool saturated, traffic will failover to compatible hosted model at reduced throughput (option to enable automatic graceful degradation)

Ramp & commit milestones tied to MAP:
- Milestone A (PoC complete): sign Letter of Intent (LoI) within 7 days of pass
- Milestone B (Staging validated): 50% of reserved commit active at contract start
- Milestone C (Production ramp): full baseline by week 8 post-contract (with weekly checkpoints)

Procurement notes: standard enterprise terms include NET30 for first invoice, DocuSign signable SOW included. If procurement needs earlier budget approval, use the attached pricing worksheet for a conservative 20% contingency.

Let us know which reserve term you prefer and we’ll prepare a draft SOW and DocuSign envelope for sign-off.

—Ben

Thanks, Ben — this is helpful. A few clarifying points from procurement and infra: 

- Budget preference: we prefer the 24-month commit if the 25% discount is firm, but we need a staged ramp so we don't overcommit capex in Q2. Can you map payments to ramp milestones (e.g., 40% first invoice, 30% at week 8, 30% at week 20)?
- Burst behavior: we need a stronger soft-burst guarantee during launches (e.g., allow +75% for up to 4 hours for launches/events) — is that negotiable as an add-on?
- Termination for convenience: procurement requests a 90-day early-termination right with pro-rated refunds for unused committed months past a 6-month minimum.

Also attaching the procurement worksheet with our internal approval steps. If we can get a revised SOW that maps payment milestones and an explicit burst addendum, I can greenlight an LoI within 72 hours.

Best,
Anya
